advisory.finding: _live_criteria_eval_available() gates 'live available' on ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY only, but the repo's plan_review model is a Bedrock model (bedrock:us.anthropic...). A Bedrock-credentialed environment (AWS creds, no ANTHROPIC/OPENAI key) has a working live backend yet is judged unavailable — so under --require-live the command exits 1 as a false 'misconfiguration', and without --require-live it silently skips a live run that would have succeeded.
scenarios: CI or a developer configured for Bedrock runs `rebar criteria eval --changed-since <ref> --require-live` and gets exit 1 despite a usable backend
Bedrock-configured local run skips the live eval and reports 'ran selection only'

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Have _run_selected_criteria_live report whether any criterion failed and make _criteria_eval_changed_since return non-zero when a live run errored (at least under --require-live).
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py:224-230 `if _live_criteria_eval_available(): _run_selected_criteria_live(...) ; return 0`
src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py:300-303 `except LLMError as exc: sys.stderr.write(...); continue` — per-criterion failure only logged
src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py:286-303 _run_selected_criteria_live returns None; no success/failure signal propagates
advisory.finding: When a live backend IS available, _run_selected_criteria_live catches each criterion's LLMError, writes it to stderr, and continues; it returns None and the caller then returns 0 unconditionally. So if every selected criterion's live calibration errors (bad fixture, provider error), the command still exits 0 — even under --require-live, which a caller sets precisely to make live-run failures visible. The check cannot distinguish 'ran and passed' from 'ran and every eval errored'.
scenarios: A rubric edit selects T8; the live provider errors on every run; the advisory job still exits 0 with only stderr noise
--require-live is set but all selected criteria fail to run — command exits 0

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Treat an empty/whitespace --changed-since as a null/absent ref (route to the no-prior-ref note) rather than falling through to the missing-id exit-2 path.
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py:128-131 `if not (args.criterion_id or "").strip(): if args.changed_since: ... return _missing_criterion_error()` — empty changed_since is falsy → missing-id path → exit 2
src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py:245-248 _is_null_ref requires len>=7 so '' is not caught as a null ref
.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml:82 `CHANGED_SINCE: ${{ ... || github.event.before }}` can resolve to an empty string
advisory.finding: An empty --changed-since value ('') is not treated as a null ref: _is_null_ref('') returns False (len<7), and the earlier guard `if args.changed_since:` is False for the empty string, so the command falls through to _missing_criterion_error() and exits 2 instead of the intended 'no prior ref' note. In the workflow, github.event.before can be empty for some events, so CHANGED_SINCE='' would exit 2 (masked only by continue-on-error).
scenarios: A push/PR event where the derived before-SHA is empty produces exit 2 (a parse-error-shaped code) rather than the documented empty-selection/exit-0 null-ref handling

The maintained owner of the CI eval-tier model no longer completely explains the eval jobs to its contributor audience.
